text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High error rate exporting traces to Honeycomb detected for service=redwood-inference-eu (trace shipper). Pager routed to @oncall-sre. Incident ID INC-2026-0423. First alert at 2026-03-15T14:02:10Z.

oncall-sre: acked. jumping in. any initial impact notes?

platform-eng: seeing a lot of 5xx from api.honeycomb.io from the trace-shipper pods in eu-west-1. pattern is spikes of 502/504 and occasional 429s. sample log lines:```
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] exporter=honeycomb pod=trace-shipper-3 status=504 msg="gateway timeout" duration=312ms
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] exporter=honeycomb pod=trace-shipper-1 status=502 msg="bad gateway"
[2026-03-15T14:02:15Z] exporter=honeycomb pod=trace-shipper-2 status=429 msg="quota exceeded"
```

observability: confirming: Honeycomb's EU ingestion graph shows a sharp drop in accepted events starting ~14:01Z, and their status page updated ~14:05Z with partial outage in "eu" region. (link: https://status.honeycomb.io/incidents/xyz)

honeycomb-status-bot: Honeycomb status update: "Investigating - EU ingestion service experiencing increased error rates. Retry/backoff recommended."

oncall-sre: probable root cause: Honeycomb ingestion instability causing our exporters to back off/queue and produce errors -> gaps in traces. immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce exporter concurrency/backoff to avoid amplifying errors 2) enable local disk buffering for shipper 3) route critical customer traces to alternate exporter/newrelic fallback (if enabled) 4) notify support and customers.

support: flagged potentially affected customers: AcmeCorp (high-sample tracing), BeamLabs. Support will open high-priority tickets and notify them we're mitigating.

oncall-sre: executing step 1 and 2 now. running command to flip exporter to buffered mode on trace-shipper deployment:```
# safer reload: set exporter to buffered mode and lower concurrency
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/trace-shipper HNY_BUFFERED=true HNY_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 && kubectl rollout restart deploy/trace-shipper
```

platform-eng: applying now in eu cluster. watching rolling pods.

(2m later)

platform-eng: rollout progressing. new pods come up with HNY_BUFFERED=true. logs show fewer 429s but still occasional 504s.

oncall-sre: started local disk buffer enabling on all shipper pods. also temporarily increased retry backoff to 30s. snippet we applied:```
exporter:
  type: honeycomb
  retries:
    max: 5
    base_delay: 5s
    max_delay: 30s
  buffered: true
  buffer_dir: /var/lib/trace-buffer
  max_concurrency: 4
```

observability: note: because of buffering, we'll see delayed spans (latency) rather than immediate loss — good for completeness but delays may affect real-time dashboards.

oncall-sre: stepping through step 3: alternate exporter. we have newrelic exporter turned on as a secondary option but it's not enabled for all services. I'm enabling for critical customers only (AcmeCorp, BeamLabs) so they keep full trace fidelity. command:```
telemetryctl route add --service redwood-inference-eu --to newrelic --filter "resource.customer in (AcmeCorp,BeamLabs)"
```

platform-eng: route applied. traffic for those customer_ids now duplicated to New Relic. verifying spans appear in new relic dashboard (awaiting confirmation).

support: update to customers: "We're aware of Honeycomb ingestion instability affecting trace exports for EU. We've enacted buffer and fallback routing to reduce data loss; some recent spans may be delayed by up to several minutes. We're monitoring and will follow up once Honeycomb confirms resolution." (sent to AcmeCorp support channel).

sre-lead: good mitigation. please collect timeline and preserve the affected pod logs and exporter configs for the postmortem. tag all artifacts with INC-2026-0423.

oncall-sre: logs archived to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-0423/ and snapshot of exporter config pushed to the incident runbook.

(handoff)

oncall-sre: handing over to @eva for next shift — I need to head to a customer call. current state: buffered exporter in place, newrelic dup route for two customers, Honeycomb still showing degraded; no data loss after buffering but delayed ingestion for ~14:01-14:10 window. ETA for full follow-up: in 30m. eva: ack, taking over.

eva: ack. I'll monitor for 1hr, keep support updated, and escalate to SRE lead if Honeycomb doesn't recover. I'll also check whether other regions might be affected.

(10m later)

honeycomb-status-bot: Update: "Partial recovery observed in EU ingestion; retries succeeding at higher rate. Customers may see delayed spans; we continue to monitor."

observability: our telemetry shows progressive recovery: accepted events back to 98% of baseline by 14:20Z. export errors decreased substantially.

support: noted some customers reported missing spans for a ~9min window; logged as incident impact. No SLO breaches for request latency but tracing completeness SLO impacted for sampled sessions.

eva: marking triage actions: 1) follow up with Honeycomb ticket and paste their incident ID 2) gather sampling windows and quantify percent of traces missing per customer 3) draft customer-facing RCA once resolved 4) slot postmortem owner. I'll assign postmortem to @sre-lead.

sre-lead: assigned. please include: timeline, config changes, why buffer wasn't previously enabled by default in eu shipper, decision tree for routing to backup exporters, and cost implications.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 status changed to "mitigated" at 2026-03-15T14:25:35Z (buffers enabled and Honeycomb returning to normal). Please keep thread updated until postmortem is posted. :white_check_mark:

support: we'll keep customers updated and include the mitigation steps in the support tickets.

eva: closing handoff notes: continuing watch for 2 hours + postmortem to follow. leaving escalations to @sre-lead.

(threads end)
